福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

神農街Shennong Street

認識狹面深厝、二樓神祕之門、許藏春的故事，還有元宵燈會和老街職人小店。

Learn about the street houses, the mysterious doors, Xu Cang-chun, and the lanterns.

這是台南最美的一條街。老屋彼此共用牆壁，誰也拆不了誰，整條街就保存下來了。它舊稱北勢街，夾在兩條港道之間。在港道淤塞之前，是全城最繁華的街道。街屋門面窄、屋身深。貨物用繩子吊上二樓存放。抬頭看！很多房子有一扇開向半空的門。是為了吊船上的貨，還是在樓上買東西？1871 年，十八歲的許藏春來這條街當學徒，後來主持商行三十多年。每到元宵，居民和學生親手彩繪燈籠，安靜的老街變成全城最亮的地方。

This is the prettiest street in Tainan. The old houses share their walls, so none of them could be torn down alone. Once called Beishi Street, it ran between two of the Five Channels. Before the silting, it was the busiest street in the city. The houses are narrow in front but very deep. Goods were hoisted by rope to the second floor. Look up! Many houses have a door opening onto thin air. Was it for cargo from the boats, or for shopping from upstairs? In 1871, Xu Cang-chun came here at eighteen to learn the trade. He ran a firm on this street for over thirty years. Every Lantern Festival, residents and students paint lanterns by hand, and the quiet street becomes the brightest in the city.

一分鐘看懂

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history
  1. 老街的樣子神農街舊稱北勢街，位於北勢港與佛頭港之間，是五條港街區的門戶。Shennong Street, once Beishi Street, was the gateway to the Five Channels district.
  2. 二樓神祕之門二樓的門圍著欄杆，卻開向半空。有兩種說法，你選哪一個？The second-floor doors open onto thin air. Pick your favorite theory.
  3. 許藏春：一個時代的抉擇泉州青年許藏春的故事，連到兩站之後的金華府。The story of Xu Cang-chun links this street to Jinhua Temple.
  4. 燈籠與職人小店元宵燈會由南臺科技大學 USR 團隊與台南市文化協會共同主辦。Every Lantern Festival, residents and students paint lanterns by hand.

認識景點

About the place

老街的樣子The old street

共用牆壁：老屋共用牆壁，誰也拆不了誰，所以整條街保存了下來。 狹面深厝：門面只有幾公尺寬，屋身卻深達百餘公尺；兩層樓、前後有門。 吊貨上樓：一樓做生意，貨物用繩索吊上二樓儲藏。 門口石塊：門口的石塊方便搬運，被兩百年的搬運磨得光亮。

shared walls: The houses share walls, so none could be torn down alone. narrow face, deep body: A few meters wide, but over a hundred meters deep. hoist: Goods were hoisted by rope to the second floor. stone blocks: Stone blocks by the doors made loading easier.

漫長的沉睡：1823 年曾文溪改道讓港口窒息，這條街沉睡了很久。 文創聚落：近年甦醒，巷弄裡擠滿工作室與手作小店。 福州杉：老屋的圓木樑常用福州杉，是從對岸福州用船運來的杉木。

A long sleep: After 1823, the harbor silted and the street fell asleep. crafts and culture: Today it is full of studios and handmade shops. Fuzhou fir: Many old houses used fir wood shipped from Fuzhou.

二樓神祕之門The mysterious doors

說法一：吊貨口：商人把船上的貨物直接經由這扇門吊進二樓貨倉。 說法二：樓上購物：婦女不便出門時，朝樓下小販喊價，再用竹籃把東西吊上去。

Theory one: cargo: Merchants hoisted cargo from the boats straight into the upstairs storerooms. Theory two: shopping: Women called down to street vendors and pulled their shopping up in a basket.

許藏春：一個時代的抉擇Xu Cang-chun's story

1871 渡海當學徒：十八歲從泉州渡海，在這條街的景祥行當學徒。 帳房到當事：七年升帳房，最後主持商務三十多年，還當上三郊的爐主。 雙重國籍：1895 年他留下入日本籍，又保留清朝原籍。 1962 女兒尋親：1917 年返鄉沒再回來；1962 年他的女兒從菲律賓來神農街打聽許家。

An apprentice at eighteen: At eighteen, he came from Quanzhou to learn the trade. Running the firm: He ran the firm for over thirty years. Dual nationals: His family became among Taiwan's first dual nationals. A daughter returns: In 1962, his daughter came from the Philippines to find the family.

燈籠與職人小店Lanterns and craft shops

燈籠：元宵是農曆年後第一個月圓之夜。 猜燈謎：走在手作燈火下，像世世代代的台南人一樣猜燈謎。 五條港行號：神農街 79 號，開在 1907 年的木造街屋。 西佛國：百年粧佛老店，看神明的臉從樟木裡浮出來。

lantern: The Lantern Festival is the first full moon of the lunar year. lantern riddles: People guess lantern riddles as they walk. Five Channels Co.: A shop in a wooden house from 1907. Xi Fo Guo: A Buddha-statue studio more than a hundred years old.

來坐畫吧：新手友善的畫畫空間，紀念品自己做。 栗子花：黃銅與天然礦石手作飾品，店貓在庭院巡邏。

Come Sit and Paint: A place to make your own souvenir. Chestnut Blossom: Handmade brass and stone jewelry.

實景照片

Photos on site

神農街 Shennong Street

神農街舊稱北勢街，是五條港區的老街。兩旁是兩層樓的老街屋，屋簷下掛滿手繪燈籠，白燈籠上寫著「神農街」。

This is Shennong Street. It was once called Beishi Street, in the old Five Channels harbor area. Two-story old shophouses line the lane, with painted lanterns under the roofs.

地上的詩 A poem in the paving

地上嵌著兩句清朝郁永河寫的詩：「渡頭更上牛車坐，日暮還過赤嵌城。」以前海水很淺，小船靠不了岸，旅客到了渡頭要改坐牛車，到傍晚才經過赤嵌城。

Two lines of an old poem are set into the street. Over three hundred years ago, Yu Yonghe wrote that the water was so shallow, boats could not reach the shore. At the landing, travelers rode ox carts, and passed Chihkan by sunset.

五條港燈籠 The Five Channels lantern

一棟老街屋，二樓是木板牆，中間有一扇小小的木格窗。其中一盞燈籠寫著「五條港」：這條街以前就在五條港的港區裡。

This old shophouse has a wooden upper floor with a small wooden window. One lantern says Five Channels, the old harbor area this street belonged to.

北勢街的石碑 A stone on Beishi Street

門邊立著一塊石碑，標題是「重修北勢街金華府碑記」。北勢街就是神農街的舊名，金華府是這條街上的一座廟。

This stone tells the story of repairing Jinhua Temple on Beishi Street, the old name of this street.

燈籠串過巷子 Lanterns across the lane

抬頭看！一串串手繪燈籠橫掛在巷子上空，兩旁是老街屋的木造二樓；右邊一棟房子的牆面是藍白色的花紋。

Look up! Strings of painted lanterns hang across the lane. On the right, one house is covered in blue-and-white patterns.

木造老屋 A wooden shophouse

抬頭看！木造老屋的二樓與手繪燈籠。

Look up! A wooden shophouse's second floor, hung with painted lanterns.

福州杉木樑 Fuzhou fir beams

抬頭看！據說屋頂這些圓圓的木樑是福州杉。清代官府禁止漢人隨便進山，山林大多是原住民的土地；當時蓋房子的杉木，很多是從福州用船運來的。

Look up! These round beams are said to be Fuzhou fir. In the Qing dynasty, settlers were not allowed to go into the mountains freely, and the forests were mostly Indigenous land. Much of the fir for houses came by ship from Fuzhou in China.

二樓的欄杆 A second-floor railing

抬頭看二樓：門前圍著一道木欄杆。神農街的老屋二樓常有門，說法有兩種：吊貨用的，或是用竹籃向小販買東西。

Look up at the second floor. A wooden railing stands in front of the upstairs doors. Was the door for cargo or for shopping?

手繪燈籠 Hand-painted lanterns

二樓欄杆前掛滿手繪燈籠，畫著山、花和各種圖案；門上方還有一盞雙魚造型的燈。

Bright hand-painted lanterns hang in front of the second-floor railing. Over the door is a lantern shaped like two fish.

鐵欄杆與九重葛 Iron balcony and bougainvillea

一棟米白色的兩層樓老房子，二樓有彎彎曲曲的紅色鐵欄杆陽台；旁邊開滿桃紅色的九重葛。

This cream-colored old house has a curvy red iron balcony. Bright pink bougainvillea grows beside it.
